deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 15% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 49% last year; 36%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $179.2B, up from $27.5B a year ago — about 2.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $13.1B, down 8% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 111% vs quarterly sales up 86% (days to collect 37 → 42). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.
Inventory up 107% vs quarterly sales up 86% (days of inventory 38 → 45). Products may be building up unsold — a warning sign in chip cycles.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 36%/yr over 3 years and 27%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 48% vs a 5-year range of 26–48% (median 39%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
